Subject: Request: sample key deletion records and retention policy for privacy audit

Hi Logan,

We're kicking off Orchid Bank's annual privacy audit and need to validate how customer encryption keys are handled when tenants request key deletion or account termination. Specifically, could you provide the following by EOD Nov 21?

- A representative sample (anonymized) of KMS key deletion events covering create/delete timestamps, operator id, and associated tenant id (if applicable). CSV preferred.
- A short description of Redwood's retention policy for key materials after deletion requests (what is retained, for how long, and how it is purged).
- Screenshots or exported logs showing the admin action in your KMS UI or the HSM audit trail provenance.

If any of these require an NDA or additional paperwork, let us know immediately. We can accept redacted samples.

Thanks,
Aisha Thompson
Orchid Bank — Security Audit

- I'll deliver the consolidated package and a short note describing the operator-id mapping and how we verify deletion (S3 lifecycle + HSM zeroization steps).

On Tue, Nov 18, 2025 at 11:02 AM, logan_wright@redwood.ai wrote:
> Hi Aisha — thanks for the clear list. Looping in Marissa (Security Solutions) and Ben (Compliance) to prepare artifacts and confirm redaction approach.

I've pulled the sample set and redaction notes. Notes for the package:
- The CSV is sampled from our deletion event stream (KMS -> HSM binding). Tenant IDs are replaced with consistent pseudo-ids to preserve event ordering but remove PII.
- Operator id is hashed; we include a mapping table for internal audit only (not shared externally).
- We include a screenshot of the HSM audit record and the KMS UI action (both redacted).
- Retention policy excerpt: Keys associated with deleted tenants are scheduled for zeroization at time of deletion; metadata (small audit marker) is retained for 90 days for investigation/rollback guardrails, then removed. We will include the quoted policy text and the config pointers (internal runbook references) in the readme.

Attachments I'll prepare: 1) 2025-11-20_kms-deletion-log-sample.csv (anonymized) 2) kms-ui-deletion-audit-screenshot.png (redacted) 3) readme-key-retention-policy.txt

If compliance wants the internal operator mapping for forensic review, Ben can arrange a secure exchange under NDA.

Marissa Cole

Hi Aisha / Orchid Bank team — attached is the package we discussed:

Attachments included:
- 2025-11-20_kms-deletion-log-sample.csv (anonymized) — sample rows with event_time, pseudo_tenant_id, action, key_id_hash, operator_id_hash, audit_ref.
- kms-ui-deletion-audit-screenshot.png — redacted view of the admin action in the KMS console and HSM audit snippet.
- readme-key-retention-policy.txt — concise explanation of retention/zeroization timeline, references to internal runbook and S3 lifecycle policies, and our redaction methodology.

Short summary:
- Deletion flow: customer request -> account ops verify -> KMS delete triggered -> HSM zeroization job invoked -> metadata audit record retained for 90 days.
- We never keep plaintext key material after zeroization; backups are rotated and purged according to the same retention timeline.
- If Orchid requires operator identity crosswalks for a specific sample, we can provide them under an NDA and a secure SFTP transfer.

For traceability we've raised SEC-4921 in our tracker (link included). Let me know if you want a short call to walk through the samples — available tomorrow morning PST.

Best,
